_meta.indication: INREBIC is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk primary or secondary (post-polycythemia vera or post-essential thrombocytopenia) myelofibrosis (MF).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1:1), double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multinational trial of two fedratinib dosing regimens (400 mg or 500 mg daily) versus placebo for at least 6 consecutive 28-day cycles.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk primary MF, post-PV MF or post-ET MF with splenomegaly, naive to JAK inhibitor treatment.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Spleen response rate, defined as the proportion of subjects with >=35% spleen volume reduction (SVR) at the end of Cycle 6 (EOC6) by MRI/CT, confirmed 4 weeks later.
pivotal_trials.result: Spleen response rate 36.5% with fedratinib 400 mg (N=96) vs 1% placebo (N=96) at EOC6 (p<0.0001); median duration of spleen response 18.2 months. Key secondary symptom response rate 40.4% vs 8.6% placebo (p<0.0001).

nct_ctgov.title: Phase III Study of SAR302503 in Intermediate-2 and High Risk Patients With Myelofibrosis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were diarrhea (66%), nausea (62%), anemia, and vomiting (39%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 21% of patients, including cardiac failure (5%) and anemia (2%); fatal cardiogenic shock occurred in 1%. Serious/fatal encephalopathy including Wernicke's occurred in 1.3% (8/608), fatal in 0.16% (1/608).
target_moa: Fedratinib is an oral kinase inhibitor with activity against wild type and mutationally activated Janus Associated Kinase 2 (JAK2) and FLT3; it reduces STAT3/5 phosphorylation, inhibits cell proliferation, and induces apoptosis, with IC50 of ~3 nM for JAK2 and greater potency for JAK2 over other JAK family members.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ENCEPHALOPATHY INCLUDING WERNICKE'S — Serious and fatal encephalopathy, including Wernicke's, has occurred in patients treated with INREBIC. Assess thiamine levels prior to and during treatment; do not start INREBIC in patients with thiamine deficiency; if encephalopathy is suspected, immediately discontinue.

orphan_indication.text: Fedratinib was granted Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of secondary and primary myelofibrosis on May 18, 2009.

basis.text: The application was designated Priority; the sponsor requested priority review asserting most patients are not eligible for allogeneic stem cell transplant, the only curative treatment for MF.

summary.text: INREBIC (fedratinib) received regular (not accelerated) approval under a Priority Review NDA based on demonstration of meaningful clinical benefit and statistically significant reduction in spleen volume and myelofibrosis-related symptoms in the Phase 3 JAKARTA trial. It had Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of secondary and primary myelofibrosis. No advisory committee meeting was held.

requirement.text: 3664-1: Conduct a randomized, concurrently controlled clinical trial comparing fedratinib 400 mg once daily to best available therapy in patients with DIPSS-intermediate-2 or high-risk MF previously treated with ruxolitinib, ensuring at least 150 subjects treated with at least 6 cycles and followed at least 3 years.

citations.quote: 3664-1 Conduct a randomized, concurrently controlled clinical trial comparing fedratinib 400 mg once daily to best available therapy in patients with DIPSS-intermediate-2 or high-risk primary myelofibrosis, post-polycythemia vera myelofibrosis, or post-essential thrombocytopenia myelofibrosis and previously treated with ruxolitinib. The trial will enroll a sufficient number of patients to ensure that at least 150 subjects are treated with at least 6 cycles of fedratinib and are followed for at least 3 years from first dose, or until death.
